title: The Step-by-Step Guide to Setting Up Sales Tax on Your Shopify Store
summary: This guide walks you through setting up Shopify sales tax. Learn to determine if you need a tax ID, how to get one and the steps to configure your setting.
body_text: Sales tax nexus: what is it? Before we get into the details, let's discuss the sales tax nexus and how it affects your ecom merce brand . Nexus used to be primarily based on physical presence. Having an office, warehouse, or even a sales representative in a state would trigger nexus. However, economic nexus has changed the game. Economic nexus means if you sell enough to customers in a state, even without a physical presence, you're responsible for collecting and remitting sales tax. Thresholds vary by state but usually involve sales volume or transaction count. For example, California's economic nexus threshold is $500,000 in sales to California customers annually. New York 's threshold is $500,000 in sales and 100 transactions. Texas ' threshold is $500,000 in sales OR 200 transactions. To track these rules, identify the states where you have the most sales and check their nexus laws. After determining where you have nexus, register for a sales tax permit in those states. Each state's process varies, so check their Department of Revenue website for instructions. Consulting companies like Numeral can integrate with your Shopify to track your sales and notify you as soon as you hit nexus in any state. The company also employs highly qualified accountants who will set up your sales tax ID in the state and start filing. How do you set up sales tax on Shopify? Let’s quickly look at the steps to set up sales tax on your Shopify website. Determining the need for a sales tax ID The first step in setting up sales tax on Shopify is determining if you need a sales tax ID. A sales tax ID, AKA a seller's or sales tax permit, is a unique number assigned to your business by your state's tax authority. It allows you to collect sales tax from your customers and remit it to the state. Whether you need a sales tax ID depends on two main factors: nexus and product taxability. If you have nexus in a state, you must collect and remit sales tax there. Along with Nexus, you must check if the product is taxable in the state. If it is, you are required to get your sales tax ID or sales tax permit in the said state. Steps to acquire a sales tax ID Once you've determined that you need a sales tax ID, the next step is to obtain one from each state where you have nexus. The process varies by state but generally involves the following: Visit the state's tax authority website. Shopify's US tax reference provides links to each state's tax authority. Look for information on registering for a sales tax permit or seller's permit. This may be under a section like " Businesses " or " Sales and Use Tax ." Follow the instructions to apply for a permit. This typically involves filling out an application, providing information about your business, and paying a fee. Once your application is approved, you'll receive your sales tax ID number. Keep this number handy, as you'll need it when setting up your tax settings in Shopify. Information you need to register your sales tax ID When applying for a sales tax ID, you must provide details about your business. While the specific requirements vary by state, here's a general list of the information you may need: Business name and address Business structure (sole proprietorship, LLC, corporation, etc.) Description of your business activities Date you started or will start selling in the state Estimated sales and/or tax liability in the state Your Social Security Number (SSN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) Personal identification information for business owners or officers Having this information ready will make the application process smoother and faster. If you need help filing sales tax and want to do it yourself, we have many guides for individual states that will guide you through the filing process step-by-step. Steps to set up sales tax on Shopify Now that you have your sales tax IDs, it's time to configure your tax settings in Shopify. Here's a step-by-step guide: 1. Log in to your Shopify admin and go to Settings > Taxes and duties . ‍ ‍ 2. In the Manage sales tax regions , click United States . ‍ ‍ 3. You’ll then see a page where you can choose to manage tax collection , see tax rates and exemptions , or create tax reports . ‍ ‍ 4. Click on the Manage Tax Collection link. You’ll see all the states you sell to, where you meet nexus thresholds, and if you have any states where you need to take action or monitor. ‍ ‍ You can click Show Details to see the nexus thresholds and how close you are to meeting them. ‍ ‍ Go to Tax Rates and Exemptions . Click on Product Category and categorize your products. ‍ ‍ For instance, you can categorize your products as apparel, software , digital goods , etc, to apply the correct tax rates. ‍ ‍ To report, click on Reporting to download tax reports. ‍ These reports show where to file sales tax and the amounts required . ‍ ‍ Any state with nexus will show under the box that says Regions you’re collecting in. Click Collect Sales Tax to start entering your sales tax ID. ‍ ‍ Select the states from the dropdown where you must collect sales tax and enter your Sales Tax ID or FEIN (aka Federal Employer Identification Number) . ‍ ‍ When adding a new product, check the box that says Charge tax on this product . ‍ ‍ If you sell to tax-exempt customers, go to Customers and uncheck the tax collection box for those customers. ‍ ‍ Go to Locations under settings. Add the locations where you ship products to ensure accurate tax collection based on origin or destination sourcing rules. And that's it! Your Shopify store is now set up to collect sales tax in the states where you have nexus. However, remember that you must also fill out individual sales tax permit forms and keep track of the nexus in each state. If you find this process overwhelming or prefer an expert to handle it, consider using Numeral . Our white-glove service takes care of all your sales tax needs, from registration to filing, so you can focus on growing your business. Best Practices for Managing Sales Tax on Shopify Setting up your sales tax settings is just the first step. To stay compliant and avoid headaches down the road, here are some best practices to keep in mind: Collecting sales tax is only part of the process . You must also file returns and regularly remit your collected tax to each state. The frequency depends on your sales volume and varies by state - some require monthly filings, while others are quarterly or annually. Filing sales tax returns involves logging into each state's tax portal , entering your sales data, and making a payment. It can be time-consuming, especially if you're registered in multiple states. Automation can help . There are a number of Shopify sales tax apps that integrate directly into the platform. White-glove services like Numeral integrate with Shopify to track your sales and automatically file returns on your behalf. They charge a fee, but the time and hassle saved can be worth it. If you prefer a hands-on approach , keep meticulous records of your sales and tax collected. Most states require you to keep this data for at least 3-4 years in case of an audit. Another aspect of compliance is product taxability . Not all products are taxed equally—some states exempt certain items like groceries or textbooks, and others have reduced rates for things like clothing or medical supplies. To ensure you're charging the correct rate for each product , use Shopify's product categorization feature. Go to Products > All products and edit each listing to assign it a tax category like "Clothing" or "Food." Then, in your tax settings, you can set specific rates for each category based on state rules. If you use Shopify's discount codes or a third-party coupon app , confirm how it interacts with your tax settings. Shopify applies discounts to the subtotal before calculating tax, but the sales tax treatment can still vary by discount type and state. See our guide to discounts, coupons, and gift card taxability to learn more. Frequently Asked Questions You definitely have questions and we have the answers. Here are a few questions our customers ask when they're trying to set up What is Shopify Tax? Shopify Tax is a built-in feature that helps automate your sales tax calculations. It uses your location and customer information to apply the appropriate tax rates to each order. Shopify Tax is included in all Shopify plans at no additional cost. Does Shopify automatically collect sales tax? No, Shopify does not automatically collect sales tax . You must set up your tax settings and enter your sales tax IDs for each state where you want to collect tax. Once you've done that, Shopify will calculate and apply the correct tax rates to orders from those states. How does Shopify calculate sales tax? Shopify calculates sales tax using a combination of your store location, customer location, and product taxability. It also considers each jurisdiction's specific tax rates and rules, including state, county, and city taxes. Some Shopify accounting software also helps with this. Can Shopify handle tax-exempt sales? Yes, Shopify can handle tax-exempt sales. If you have customers exempt from sales tax, such as resellers or non-profit organizations, you can mark their customer profile as tax-exempt in Shopify. This will prevent the tax from being applied to their orders. What happens if I add a new product or expand my business to a new state? If you add a new product, categorize it correctly in Shopify for tax purposes. If the product is exempt from sales tax or subject to a reduced rate, you may need to set up a tax override. If you expand your business to a new state and establish a nexus there, you must register for a sales tax ID and add it to your Shopify tax settings. This ensures you collect and remit tax correctly for orders from that state. When and how should I remit sales tax? The frequency and method of remitting sales tax varies by state. Some states require monthly filings, while others are quarterly or annual. You'll need to check the specific requirements for each state where you're registered. To file your sales tax returns, log in to the state's tax portal and enter the total sales and tax collected for the filing period. You'll then pay the tax due via ACH transfer or credit card. If you find the filing process time-consuming or confusing, consider using Numeral. Our automated filing service ensures that your returns are filed accurately and on time, with no action needed. Is shipping taxable, and how does Shopify handle that? The taxability of shipping varies by state. Some states consider shipping charges part of the item's taxable price, while others treat it as a separate, non-taxable service. In Shopify, you can choose whether to charge shipping tax in each state where you collect tax. By default, Shopify will apply the state's rules for shipping taxability, but you can override this setting if needed. Build a sales tax compliant ecommerce brand with Numeral This guide covers a lot, from nexus to product taxability to filing frequency. It's a lot to digest, but taking it one step at a time is critical. Start by determining where you have nexus and registering for permits. Then, configure your Shopify settings to collect the right amount of tax from each customer. Stay on top of filing deadlines and consider automating the process. If you're overwhelmed or want peace of mind, you can partner with Numeral . Our white-glove service covers everything from registration to filing, so you can stay compliant without lifting a finger.

title: Tipos de actividades económicas en Colombia: clasificación
summary: Cuando alguien busca "tipos de actividades económicas en Colombia" casi siempre está preguntando por dos cosas distintas al mismo tiempo, sin darse cuenta: por un lado, la clasificación general que enseña cualquier curso de economía (sector primario, secundario, terciario)
body_text: Cuando alguien busca "tipos de actividades económicas en Colombia" casi siempre está preguntando por dos cosas distintas al mismo tiempo, sin darse cuenta: por un lado, la clasificación general que enseña cualquier curso de economía (sector primario, secundario, terciario); por otro, el código CIIU específico que la DIAN exige registrar en el RUT para poder facturar, declarar renta o pagar el impuesto de Industria y Comercio. Dos niveles de clasificación que conviene no confundir Clasificación económica por sectores: agrupa las actividades según la naturaleza del proceso productivo (extraer materia prima, transformarla, prestar un servicio). Es la clasificación que se usa para análisis macroeconómico y para entender la estructura productiva de un país. Clasificación CIIU (Clasificación Industrial Internacional Uniforme): es el sistema de códigos oficial, adoptado por el DANE y usado por la DIAN, las cámaras de comercio y los municipios, que identifica con precisión la actividad económica de una persona natural o jurídica para fines tributarios, estadísticos y de registro mercantil. Ambas están relacionadas —cada sección del CIIU corresponde, en términos generales, a uno de los sectores económicos clásicos—, pero cumplen funciones distintas: una es conceptual, la otra es un requisito legal concreto. Clasificación general por sectores económicos Sector Qué agrupa Ejemplos Secciones CIIU relacionadas Primario Extracción y obtención de materias primas directamente de la naturaleza Agricultura, ganadería, pesca, silvicultura, minería, extracción de petróleo Sección A (Agricultura, ganadería, caza, silvicultura y pesca), Sección B (Explotación de minas y canteras) Secundario Transformación de materias primas en productos elaborados Manufactura, construcción, generación de energía Sección C (Industrias manufactureras), Sección D (Electricidad, gas, vapor), Sección F (Construcción) Terciario Prestación de servicios que no producen bienes físicos Comercio, transporte, educación, salud, servicios financieros, turismo Secciones G a S (comercio, transporte, alojamiento, información, financieras, inmobiliarias, profesionales, administrativas, educación, salud, entretenimiento, otros servicios) Cuaternario (categoría emergente, no siempre reconocida de forma oficial) Actividades intensivas en conocimiento y tecnología Desarrollo de software, investigación y desarrollo, consultoría especializada, inteligencia artificial Principalmente dentro de la Sección J (Información y comunicaciones) y la Sección M (Actividades profesionales, científicas y técnicas) El llamado "sector cuaternario" no es una categoría oficial dentro del CIIU colombiano, pero cada vez se usa más en el análisis económico para separar las actividades de conocimiento intensivo (tecnología, I+D) de los servicios tradicionales, dado su peso creciente en la economía. ¿Qué es el código CIIU y quién lo administra? El CIIU es la Clasificación Industrial Internacional Uniforme de todas las actividades económicas, un sistema desarrollado originalmente por las Naciones Unidas y adaptado para Colombia por el DANE (actualmente en su versión CIIU Rev. 4 A.C. , actualizada en 2020 mediante ajustes de mantenimiento). La DIAN adoptó esta clasificación mediante la Resolución 000139 de 2012 , con una actualización posterior mediante la Resolución 000114 de 2020 , y exige su registro obligatorio en el RUT para efectos de control tributario, aduanero y cambiario. Su propósito no es solo tributario: también sirve para que el DANE y otras entidades produzcan estadísticas económicas comparables a nivel nacional e internacional, agrupando empresas y personas según procesos productivos similares. La estructura jerárquica del código CIIU (algo que casi nadie explica bien) La mayoría de guías muestran el código CIIU como un número de cuatro dígitos sin explicar cómo se construye esa jerarquía. En realidad, el CIIU tiene cuatro niveles, cada uno más específico que el anterior: Sección — identificada con una letra (A a U), agrupa el conjunto más amplio de actividades (por ejemplo, la Sección J: Información y comunicaciones). División — dos dígitos, agrupa actividades más afines dentro de la sección (por ejemplo, la división 62: Desarrollo de sistemas informáticos, consultoría y actividades relacionadas). Grupo — tres dígitos, un nivel más específico dentro de la división. Clase — cuatro dígitos, el nivel más detallado, que es justamente el código que se registra en el RUT. Ejemplo descompuesto: el código 6201 (Actividades de desarrollo de sistemas informáticos) , uno de los más registrados en Colombia, se descompone así: Nivel Código Descripción Sección J Información y comunicaciones División 62 Desarrollo de sistemas informáticos (planificación, análisis, diseño, programación, pruebas), consultoría informática y actividades relacionadas Grupo 620 Actividades de desarrollo de sistemas informáticos, consultoría informática y actividades relacionadas Clase 6201 Actividades de desarrollo de sistemas informáticos (planificación, análisis, diseño, programación, pruebas) Entender esta jerarquía ayuda a elegir el código correcto cuando la actividad de una empresa no encaja perfectamente en una sola clase: conviene revisar primero la sección y la división más afines, y luego bajar al nivel de clase más preciso, en lugar de adivinar directamente un código de cuatro dígitos. Las 21 secciones del CIIU en Colombia Sección Nombre Divisiones A Agricultura, ganadería, caza, silvicultura y pesca 01 a 03 B Explotación de minas y canteras 05 a 09 C Industrias manufactureras 10 a 33 D Suministro de electricidad, gas, vapor y aire acondicionado 35 E Distribución de agua; evacuación de aguas residuales, gestión de desechos y saneamiento ambiental 36 a 39 F Construcción 41 a 43 G Comercio al por mayor y al por menor; reparación de vehículos 45 a 47 H Transporte y almacenamiento 49 a 53 I Alojamiento y servicios de comida 55 a 56 J Información y comunicaciones 58 a 63 K Actividades financieras y de seguros 64 a 66 L Actividades inmobiliarias 68 M Actividades profesionales, científicas y técnicas 69 a 75 N Actividades de servicios administrativos y de apoyo 77 a 82 O Administración pública y defensa; seguridad social de afiliación obligatoria 84 P Educación 85 Q Actividades de atención de la salud humana y de asistencia social 86 a 88 R Actividades artísticas, de entretenimiento y recreación 90 a 93 S Otras actividades de servicios 94 a 96 T Actividades de los hogares individuales como empleadores o productores para uso propio 97 a 98 U Actividades de organizaciones y entidades extraterritoriales 99 Por qué el código CIIU no es solo un trámite administrativo Este es el punto que casi ningún artículo desarrolla con suficiente detalle: registrar el código CIIU correcto tiene consecuencias tributarias directas, no es un simple dato de formulario. Define la tarifa de autorretención especial de renta: las empresas responsables de esta autorretención calculan la tarifa aplicable según el CIIU registrado, con porcentajes que varían según el sector (por ejemplo, entre 0,55 % y 4,50 %, según la actividad). Determina la tarifa del impuesto de Industria y Comercio (ICA): cada municipio establece tarifas distintas de ICA según la actividad económica declarada, de modo que un código CIIU mal elegido puede hacer que pagues una tarifa distinta a la que realmente corresponde a tu negocio. Afecta la clasificación estadística que usa el DANE para medir la estructura productiva del país, algo relevante si tu empresa participa en encuestas o censos económicos oficiales. Puede generar una alerta de fiscalización si la actividad registrada no coincide con la actividad real que se evidencia en las facturas emitidas, los ingresos declarados o los movimientos bancarios de la empresa. Determina qué normativa sectorial específica aplica (por ejemplo, ciertas actividades financieras, de salud o de educación tienen regulaciones y reportes adicionales asociados a su clasificación). Cómo elegir y registrar tu código CIIU: paso a paso Identifica tu actividad económica principal: la que genera la mayor proporción de tus ingresos durante el año gravable, no necesariamente la primera que se te ocurra o la más conocida. Busca por palabra clave o por código en el buscador de tu Cámara de Comercio o en el listado oficial del DANE, en lugar de adivinar un código de memoria. Verifica la descripción completa de la clase , no solo el nombre corto, para confirmar que efectivamente describe lo que hace tu negocio. Registra hasta tres códigos si es necesario: el RUT permite registrar una actividad principal (casilla 46) y hasta dos actividades secundarias (casillas 48 y 50), si tu empresa realmente desarrolla más de una actividad relevante. Verifica el código en el sistema Muisca de la DIAN al momento de diligenciar o actualizar el RUT, para confirmar que corresponde a la versión CIIU vigente. Actualiza el RUT si tu actividad principal cambia con el tiempo , ya que el código no se ajusta automáticamente; es responsabilidad del contribuyente mantenerlo actualizado. Códigos especiales que no son CIIU estándar Un detalle que muy pocas fuentes explican es que la DIAN usa, además de los códigos CIIU tradicionales, algunos códigos exclusivos para personas naturales en situaciones específicas que no representan actividades productivas en sentido estricto: 0010 — Empleado asalariado (no se usa el CIIU del sector donde trabaja, sino este código específico). 0020 — Pensionado. 0082 — Rentista de capital. Estos códigos existen porque el RUT también aplica a personas naturales que no desarrollan una actividad empresarial propiamente dicha, pero que igual deben identificarse fiscalmente ante la DIAN. Errores comunes al clasificar la actividad económica Elegir el código más popular o genérico en lugar del que describe con precisión la actividad real (por ejemplo, usar "comercio al por menor no especializado" cuando existe una clase más específica para el producto que se vende). No actualizar el código cuando cambia el negocio principal , dejando registrada una actividad que ya no refleja la fuente real de ingresos. Confundir actividad principal con secundaria , reportando como principal una actividad que genera menos ingresos que otra registrada como secundaria. Usar el CIIU del sector en el que se trabaja como empleado , cuando en realidad corresponde el código 0010 (empleado asalariado). No verificar la tarifa de ICA municipal asociada al código elegido , lo que puede derivar en pagos de más o de menos frente a lo que realmente corresponde. Registrar demasiadas actividades secundarias sin relevancia real , complicando innecesariamente el perfil tributario de la empresa. Preguntas frecuentes ¿Es obligatorio tener un código CIIU en Colombia? Sí, toda persona natural o jurídica que se registre en el RUT ante la DIAN debe indicar al menos un código CIIU correspondiente a su actividad económica principal. ¿Puedo tener más de una actividad económica registrada? Sí, el RUT permite registrar una actividad principal y hasta dos actividades económicas secundarias, si el negocio efectivamente las desarrolla. ¿Qué pasa si elijo un código CIIU incorrecto? Puede generar inconsistencias frente a la DIAN, aplicación de una tarifa de ICA o de autorretención distinta a la que corresponde, y en casos de discrepancia notoria entre la actividad declarada y la real, puede derivar en procesos de fiscalización. ¿El sector cuaternario es una categoría oficial en Colombia? No dentro de la clasificación CIIU oficial; es un concepto usado más en análisis económico para diferenciar actividades intensivas en conocimiento y tecnología, que en el CIIU quedan distribuidas principalmente entre las secciones J y M. ¿Con qué frecuencia debo revisar mi código CIIU? No hay una periodicidad obligatoria, pero se recomienda revisarlo cada vez que cambie la actividad principal de la empresa o al momento de la renovación anual del registro mercantil ante la Cámara de Comercio.

title: 10 Best Period Underwear (That Are Also HSA/FSA Eligible)
summary: Compare the 10 best period underwear, their health and cost benefits, and how to determine if you’re eligible to buy them using your HSA or FSA funds.
body_text: Period underwear has quickly become one of the most popular reusable menstrual care products because it offers comfortable, leak-resistant protection while helping reduce waste and long-term period care costs. They don’t have to fully replace tampons and pads either. In some cases, period underwear can provide additional protection, overnight comfort, or simply give you peace of mind. Even if you don’t plan on fully replacing tampons and pads, period underwear can make a great addition to your menstrual care routine. Many period and menstrual care products are also eligible expenses under Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) and Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs) , which means you may be able to use pre-tax healthcare dollars to purchase them. This guide to choosing the best pair for you will cover these topics to help you make your decision: How does period underwear work and what are the benefits of using it? 10 benefits of using period underwear over pads, tampons, cups, and other menstrual products How much money can one pair of period underwear save you? How to choose the best period underwear for your needs 10 best period underwear for a variety of health concerns, with different fits Is period underwear HSA or FSA eligible? 8 tips to extend the life of your period underwear Before we get to where and how to buy HSA/FSA eligible period underwear , let’s start by looking at how period underwear works and what the core benefits are. How does period underwear work and what are the benefits of using it? Period underwear offers a reusable alternative to traditional menstrual products like pads and tampons, while still providing absorbent leak protection throughout your cycle. As these products become more popular, many people are curious about how they actually work, what benefits they offer, and whether they’re worth the investment. How long does period underwear last? Most high-quality period underwear lasts between 2 and 5 years with proper care. The lifespan depends on the brand, fabric quality, how often you wear them, and how carefully you wash and dry them. The absorbent layers inside period underwear naturally wear down over time. After repeated washes, the fabric may become less effective at absorbing fluid or preventing leaks. As with normal underwear, elastic bands and seams can also stretch out with regular use. Your flow can also affect longevity. Heavier flows may put more strain on absorbent layers over time compared to occasional light spotting use. How often should you buy new period underwear? Most people should plan to replace period underwear every 1 to 3 years, depending on usage and care habits. If you use period underwear heavily throughout every cycle, you may need to replace certain pairs sooner. There’s no universal replacement schedule because everyone’s menstrual routine looks different. Some people only use period underwear as backup protection, while others wear it exclusively during their period. A good approach is to evaluate your underwear at the end of each year and look for signs of wear or reduced absorbency. You may want to buy new period underwear more often if you use the same pair every cycle without rotating, you frequently wear heavy-flow styles overnight, you accidentally machine dry them on high heat, you notice leaks developing, and the fit changes over time. Many people find it helpful to own enough pairs for at least 2 to 3 days of wear before washing. That usually means having between 4 and 8 pairs, depending on your flow and laundry schedule. Replacing one or two pairs at a time instead of your entire collection can help spread out costs and keep your period care routine consistent. Proper washing and maintenance also play a major role in how frequently you’ll need to replace your period underwear, so caring for them correctly can save money over time. What’s the best way to wash period underwear? The best way to wash period underwear is to rinse it in cold water after use, then machine wash on a gentle cycle without fabric softener or bleach. Air drying is usually the safest option to help preserve the absorbent layers. Most brands include specific washing instructions, but the general care process stays fairly similar across products. Here’s a simple step-by-step routine for washing period underwear: Rinse after wearing: Rinse the underwear in cold water until the water runs mostly clear. This helps remove excess blood before washing. Place in a laundry bag: Using a mesh laundry bag can help protect delicate fabrics and elastic during the wash cycle. Wash in cold water: Choose a gentle cycle with mild detergent. Hot water can damage absorbent materials and shorten the lifespan of the underwear. Avoid fabric softener and bleach: Fabric softeners can coat absorbent fibers and reduce performance. Bleach may weaken fabrics and elastic over time. Air dry when possible: Lay flat or hang dry. High heat from dryers can damage leak-resistant layers and reduce absorbency. Some people prefer hand washing period underwear, especially for delicate fabrics, but most modern brands are machine washable. You should also avoid ironing or dry cleaning period underwear because heat and chemicals can damage the specialized layers inside the fabric. If odor becomes an issue, a small amount of white vinegar during washing may help remove buildup naturally without damaging absorbency. Proper care matters because the technology inside period underwear depends on specialized fabrics staying intact. Consistent washing habits can help preserve leak protection and extend the usable life of each pair. The easier the care routine feels, the more likely you are to stick with reusable menstrual products long term. 10 benefits of using period underwear over pads, tampons, cups, and other menstrual products Period underwear has become increasingly popular because it offers a reusable, comfortable, and low-maintenance alternative to traditional menstrual products. While pads, tampons, and menstrual cups still work well for many people, period underwear provides several unique benefits that can make managing your cycle easier and more convenient. Here are some of the biggest advantages of using period underwear: Improved comfort — Period underwear often feels more like regular underwear than bulky pads or internal menstrual products, which can make all-day wear more comfortable. Cost savings over time — Although the upfront cost may be higher (especially if you plan on buying multiple pairs to start), reusable period underwear can replace hundreds of disposable pads or tampons over its lifespan, helping reduce long-term menstrual care expenses. HSA/FSA eligible — Many period underwear products qualify as HSA- and FSA-eligible menstrual care expenses, which means you may be able to use pre-tax healthcare dollars to purchase them through online marketplaces like Flex . Less skin irritation — Soft, breathable fabrics may help reduce chafing, dryness, and irritation that some people experience with disposable pads or tampons. Fewer added chemicals — Many period underwear brands focus on reusable fabric construction without fragrances or unnecessary additives commonly found in some disposable menstrual products. Eco-friendly and sustainable — Reusable period underwear helps reduce waste by replacing disposable pads, liners, and tampons that would otherwise be thrown away each month. Leak protection — Many period underwear styles include built-in leak-resistant layers and extended coverage areas designed to help prevent visible leaks during the day or overnight. Lower risk of toxic shock syndrome (TSS) — Because period underwear is worn externally, it does not carry the same TSS concerns associated with tampon use. Versatility and convenience — Period underwear can work for light spotting, heavy flow days, overnight protection, workouts, travel, postpartum recovery, and backup protection alongside other menstrual products. Already wearing it — Instead of needing to carry pads or tampons everywhere you go, you’re already wearing period underwear, so you’re already prepared for what comes your way. That can make unexpected periods, long workdays, travel, or busy schedules feel much less stressful. As more people look for reusable menstrual care options, period underwear continues to stand out as a flexible and cost-effective choice for everyday period management. One pair of period underwear can potentially replace hundreds of disposable pads or tampons over its lifespan, which may save you anywhere from $50 to $200 or more over time depending on your menstrual routine. Most period underwear brands estimate their products last between 40 and 60 washes, though many users report getting several years of use with proper care. If you wear one pair during every cycle, that single pair could replace dozens of disposable products each year. For example: A medium-absorbency pair may replace about 2 to 5 regular tampons or pads per wear If worn 50 times over its lifespan, one pair could replace roughly 100 to 250 disposable products Disposable pads and tampons often cost between $0.20 and $0.50 each depending on brand and type That means one pair of reusable period underwear could offset approximately: $20 to $125 in disposable product costs over time Even more if you typically buy premium organic or specialty menstrual products The savings can add up faster for people with heavier flows or longer cycles who normally use more disposable products each month. Period underwear may also help you avoid emergency purchases when traveling or during unexpected cycles, which can sometimes cost more at convenience stores or pharmacies. If you build a small rotation of several pairs, you may reduce your need for disposable menstrual products almost entirely. Buying just 5 pairs would cost you $125 dollars. Even if each period costs you $10 in tampons and pads, you’d end up spending $120 in just one year. Your actual savings will depend on your flow, how frequently you wash them, and the overall wear they receive, but the right rotation of reusable pairs can save you a meaningful amount over the life of each product. How to choose the best period underwear for your needs Choosing the best period underwear starts with understanding your flow, comfort preferences, and how you plan to use them throughout your cycle. With so many absorbency levels, styles, and specialty features now available, comparing the right factors can help you find period underwear that feels comfortable, performs reliably, and fits your everyday routine. What types of period underwear exist? Period underwear comes in a range of styles and fits, but the most common type breakdown is based largely on absorbency levels. Light & Liner: These styles are designed for spotting, very light flow days, or backup protection with tampons or menstrual cups. Moderate: Moderate absorbency period underwear works well for average daytime flow and can often replace several pads or tampons on medium-flow days. Heavy: Heavy absorbency styles provide extra leak protection for heavier periods and typically include thicker absorbent layers. Overnight: Overnight period underwear offers extended front and back coverage to help prevent leaks while sleeping. Sport & Activewear: Athletic period underwear uses breathable, moisture-wicking fabrics designed to stay comfortable during workouts and physical activity. How to evaluate the features of a pair of period underwear Not all period underwear is designed the same way, so comparing the right features can help you find a pair that matches your flow, comfort preferences, and lifestyle. Here are the most important things to evaluate before buying. Absorbency level: Choose a pair with enough absorbency for your flow, whether you need light spotting protection or heavy overnight coverage. You may want different pairs for different days of your period. Leak protection coverage: Look for styles with extended front, back, or side coverage if you want extra protection against leaks. You can also cover some of these gaps by occasionally using tampons or pads. Fabric and comfort: Soft, breathable fabrics like cotton or moisture-wicking blends usually feel more comfortable for all-day wear. Non-toxic, PFAS-free materials: Some period underwear has historically been made with PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, sometimes called “forever chemicals”). If material safety matters to you, look for brands that advertise PFAS-free construction or carry third-party certifications like OEKO-TEX STANDARD 100. Fit and sizing: A snug but comfortable fit helps prevent leaks and keeps the absorbent layers close to your body. It not only enhances comfort, but ensures the product works as intended. Odor control: Many brands include moisture-wicking or odor-resistant materials to help you stay fresh throughout the day, supporting hygiene and increasing comfort. Washability: The best period underwear should be easy to rinse, machine wash, and maintain without complicated care instructions. Durability: High-quality pairs with reinforced seams and strong elastic often last longer and provide better long-term value. Period underwear needs to hold up to regular wear and routine cleaning. Style and cut: Period underwear comes in styles like bikini, brief, thong, boyshort, and high-waisted fits to match different comfort preferences and outfits. Material safety is worth a closer look. Period underwear sits against sensitive skin for hours at a time, and past testing has found PFAS in some products, so choosing brands that are transparent about PFAS-free construction and certifications gives you extra peace of mind alongside comfort and performance. It’s all about finding the right fit for your needs. That could mean five identical pairs or a mix of light, medium, and heavy pairs that you wear at different times. Ultimately, it’s about balancing performance, comfort, and confidence. What do you gain as you spend more money on a pair of period underwear? More expensive period underwear often includes higher-quality materials, stronger absorbency technology, and features designed for better comfort and durability. While budget-friendly options can still work well, premium pairs may feel more comfortable and last longer with regular use. Is period underwear HSA or FSA eligible? Yes, many types of period underwear are HSA- and FSA-eligible because menstrual care products qualify as eligible medical expenses under current IRS guidelines. That means you may be able to use funds from your Health Savings Account (HSA) or Flexible Spending Account (FSA) to purchase qualifying period underwear, reusable pads, liners, and other menstrual products. In some cases, period underwear that serves a dual purpose may need a Letter of Medical Necessity (LMN) to qualify. Typically though, period underwear automatically qualifies as a menstrual care product. Eligibility can vary by retailer and product type, so it’s helpful to shop through platforms like the Flex Marketplace, which makes it easier to find HSA and FSA-eligible menstrual care products online . Many merchants let you buy directly with your HSA/FSA payment card instead of paying out of pocket. 8 tips to extend the life of your period underwear Period underwear can last for years with proper care, but washing and storing it incorrectly can shorten its lifespan and reduce absorbency. Following a few simple maintenance habits can help you get better performance, prevent leaks, and save more money over time. Rinse them after use— Rinsing period underwear in cold water soon after wearing helps remove excess blood and prevents buildup in the absorbent layers. Wash with cold water— Cold water is gentler on absorbent fabrics and helps preserve the leak-resistant technology inside the underwear. Skip fabric softener— Fabric softeners can coat absorbent fibers and make period underwear less effective over time. Avoid bleach— Bleach may damage elastic, weaken fabric, and reduce the lifespan of the absorbent lining. Air dry whenever possible— High dryer heat can break down leak-proof layers and shorten the life of your underwear. Use a gentle detergent— Mild detergents help clean the fabric without causing unnecessary wear or irritation. Rotate between multiple pairs— Owning several pairs reduces how often each one gets washed and can help them last longer. Follow the brand’s care instructions— Different materials and absorbency technologies may require specific washing or drying recommendations. Taking proper care of your period underwear can help maintain absorbency, improve comfort, and extend the value of your purchase over time. In summary Period underwear offers a comfortable, reusable, and increasingly popular alternative to traditional menstrual products, with options available for everything from light spotting to heavy overnight protection. Whether you prioritize comfort, leak prevention, sustainability, or convenience, there are now period underwear styles designed to fit almost every lifestyle and menstruation concern. As you compare products, pay close attention to absorbency, fit, fabric quality, and care instructions so you can choose a pair that works well for your flow and daily routine. Investing in high-quality period underwear may also help reduce long-term menstrual care costs, especially since many products qualify as HSA- and FSA-eligible expenses. title: 07/02/2024 Mastering OKRs: Is losing weight an Objective or a Key Result? **What are OKRs in the first place?** First of all, let’s start from the beginning and explain...
body_text: 07/02/2024 Mastering OKRs: Is losing weight an Objective or a Key Result? by Luiz Corandin is - Programme Manager and an OKR Coach Agility OKRs What are OKRs in the first place? First of all, let’s start from the beginning and explain what this methodology called OKRs is. OKRs (Objectives and Key Results) is a goal-setting framework used by organizations and individuals to define and measure their objectives. Objectives are qualitative, aspirational goals, while Key Results are specific, measurable outcomes that indicate progress. This approach fosters alignment and transparency at various levels within an organization, from company-wide goals to team contributions. Regular check-ins ensure focus and adaptability, creating a dynamic system for achieving and celebrating success. OKRs promote transparency, collaboration, alignment and agility in goal pursuit. As we entered a hypergrowth phase, it became urgent to adopt an intentional way to set and track goals. We use OKR to focus on the right direction (Do the right things), align on the right things (Do things right) and making fast decisions autonomously (Do things fast). Starting with the Why When coaching on OKRs, I often notice individuals start setting their OKRs (Objective and key results) by discussing tasks, action plans and initiatives. Few can easily connect these solutions with outcomes, and even fewer can explain why they engage in those initiatives in the first place. If this resonates with you, know that many share the same experience. In his Golden Circle theory, Simon Sinek explained how we are programmed to communicate. We’re used to expressing WHAT we do instead of WHY we do things. Moreover, we spend much time discussing solutions like products, services, and ideas (outputs), neglecting the reasons behind these solutions. Simon mentioned that leading companies communicate from the inside-out, starting with why they exist, then how they function, and finally, what they do. The field of Neuroscience highlights the importance of always starting your message by stating your purpose. When presenting your WHY, you activate the part of the brain that activates behaviors — Prefrontal Cortex. Starting with the why helps us uncover the true purpose and objectives of a task. This in turn, might transform how we motivate people to pursue more meaningful goals towards making Africans’ lives easier than just “developing a new feature”. Objective & Key Results — Real-life example When I guide Product and Tech teams at Yassir in setting significant objectives and Key Results, I often ask them if “losing weight” is considered an Objective or a Key Result. Generally, individuals respond by identifying it as an objective. The reason for this is, as humans, we usually perceive goals like “Getting in shape, losing a few pounds, gaining muscles…etc” as more tangible and measurable. Following that, I ask another question “Why would someone try to lose weight?” Responses come in like this: To play around with their kids without feeling tired To lace their shoes without struggling To increase their self-esteem To have better health and live longer Setting goals focused only on gaining muscles and losing weight may not be that inspiring after a while and would likely lead to giving up in the middle of the journey. However, when we design our metrics to be focused on deeper reasons behind the goal, we send a strong message to our brain: “It is important to keep going to the gym because we are tired of not being able to lace our shoes properly”. Setting OKRs using the Golden Circle model To stimulate the part of the brain that controls behaviors, we can take inspiration from the Golden Circle model, starting with the objective instead of the key results or tasks. This involves: The clarity of our objective (WHY) The discipline of tracking our key results (HOW) The consistency of what we are doing to reach it (WHAT) Returning to the example of getting in shape and setting a personal OKR by using the same approach above, we might have: Objective: Become healthier than ever to be able to play with my kids KR1: Lose weight from 85 kg to 80 kg KR2: Decrease my body fat percentage from 27% to 22% KR3: Reduce my waist circumference from 104 cm to 94 cm Objective: Enhance my running performance to complete Berlin’s Ultramarathon KR1: Achieve an average pace of 5:30’’/km during training. KR2: Lose weight from 75 kg to 72kg KR3: Increase my VO² max from 65 to 75 mL/kg/min Both examples share the goal of losing weight, but their action plans (tasks) may vary based on the underlying context (reason). Someone aiming to shed pounds for better health might establish tasks like reducing sugar and carbohydrate intake, whereas an individual focused on improving running performance may set goals such as increasing exercise frequency or hiring a professional coach. The crucial factor is must align our initiatives with the underlying motivation (WHY); failure to do so may lead us in the wrong direction. Takeaways Many teams struggle with OKR implementations due to the inability to change how they work. While new frameworks or tools can help, changing the way we approach our goals and tasks can make significant improvements in our work results. What I learned at Yassir is that prioritizing purpose in setting OKRs proved to be effective. Having a narrative that mobilizes and a clear and detailed reason simplifies tasks and makes them more straightforward toward the goal. As the OKR framework continues to gain prominence in the start-up world, OKR practitioners and champions are asked to be outstanding storytellers who can articulate a compelling vision for why we do what we do (be it losing weight or otherwise).
